title: Quote card
summary: Type design: a serif quotation with a giant decorative quote mark and a small-caps byline.
brief: Style the quote as a card: a #fff7ed background, a 6px #f97316 bar down the left, 12px rounded corners and padding of 40px on top, 32px on the sides and 28px at the bottom.

A huge “ mark (Georgia, 96px, line-height 1, #fdba74) sits behind the text, 8px above the card’s top edge and 20px from its left edge. The quote is Georgia, 26px, italic, line-height 1.3, #431407, and is drawn over the mark.
The byline is 16px below: system-ui, 13px, semibold, uppercase, 0.15em letter-spacing, #c2410c, and starts with an em dash and a space that are not in the text.
hints: The quote mark is not in the markup: it is .quote::before with content: "“". Give .quote position: relative and the mark position: absolute with top: -8px and left: 20px.
Absolutely positioned boxes paint over normal text. Give .quote-text position: relative too, and since it comes later in the page it is drawn on top of the mark.
The dash is .author::before { content: "— "; }. Uppercase and wide letter-spacing make the byline read like small caps.

children.text: Make it work, make it right, make it fast.

solutionNotes: Two fonts with clear jobs: a serif italic for the voice of the quote, a small, spaced-out sans for the label. The decorative mark lives in ::before, so the text stays clean for copying and screen readers. Positioned elements paint above unpositioned ones, so the mark would cover the quote; giving the quote position: relative puts it in the same layer, and being later in the page, it wins.
